title: Humidity: Water in the Air
summary: How water evaporates into the air as invisible water vapor, why warm air holds more of it, how cooling makes dew and clouds, and why humid days feel hotter.
poll: A humid day is harder to bear than a dry day of the same heat.

versions.title: Water in the Air
versions.text:
Lick your hand. Now blow on it. It feels cool. The wet spot dries up. Where did the water go? It went up into the air!

Air has water in it. You can not see it. The water is a gas. This gas is called water vapor.

Water goes up from the sea. It goes up from lakes. It goes up from plants and wet clothes, too.

Some days the air has a lot of vapor. Then we say the air is humid. Some days the air has just a bit. Then the air is dry.

Warm air can hold more vapor than cold air. When air cools, the vapor turns back into drops. At night, the grass gets cold. Drops form on it. That is dew. Clouds form this way, too.

On hot days, you sweat. Sweat dries on your skin. That cools you. But in humid air, sweat dries slow. So you feel hot and wet.

Riyadh is far from the sea. Its air is dry. Jeddah is by the sea. Its air is humid. A tool can tell us how humid the air is.

versions.text:

Air always has some water in it, even when the sky is clear. This water is not in drops. It is a gas that you can not see, called water vapor. The amount of water vapor in the air is called humidity.

Water gets into the air when it evaporates, which means it changes from a liquid into a gas. Water evaporates from seas, lakes, and rivers. It also evaporates from the leaves of plants, from puddles, and from wet clothes on a line.

Warm air can hold more water vapor than cold air. When air cools, some vapor must condense, or turn back into tiny drops. On a cool night, grass gets cold, and by morning it is covered with drops called dew. Clouds and fog form in the same way.

Scientists use a number called relative humidity. It compares how much vapor the air holds with the most it could hold. At 100 percent, the air is full.

Humidity changes how we feel. When you are hot, your body makes sweat, and as the sweat evaporates, it takes heat away from your skin. In humid air, sweat evaporates slowly, so a humid day feels hotter and stickier.

Riyadh is far from the sea, so its air is often dry. Jeddah and Dammam are on the coast, so their summers are humid. Experts measure humidity with a tool called a hygrometer.

versions.text:

Instead, it has migrated directly into the surrounding ambient atmosphere, where it continues existing persistently in an invisible gaseous form that professional meteorologists investigate systematically with considerable methodological care and precision.

Ambient atmospheric air invariably and universally contains at least some measurable quantity of water, even when the overhead sky appears perfectly transparent and entirely cloudless, because water can exist naturally and stably as a gas formally termed water vapor. Within this particular gaseous molecular state, individual water molecules drift independently and continuously among the considerably more numerous surrounding molecules of nitrogen and oxygen that collectively constitute the overwhelming majority of our planet's atmosphere, and the overall quantity of vapor present within the air at any given moment is formally and technically known as humidity. Even the most persistently arid desert air typically contains at least a small residual quantity of water vapor under virtually all conditions.

Water fundamentally and continuously enters the surrounding atmosphere through the process of evaporation, the specific underlying physical process by which any liquid substance transforms directly into a corresponding gaseous state. Every single day without exception, truly enormous and almost incomprehensible quantities of water evaporate continuously from oceans, lakes, and rivers worldwide, while additional ambient moisture simultaneously escapes from the leaves of surrounding vegetation, from residual puddles remaining after a rainstorm, and from laundry drying gradually under direct sunshine, meaning the air situated directly above a warm sea consequently and predictably gains far more moisture overall than equivalent air positioned above a comparatively arid desert region.

It is raining very hard and the streets are full of water
The air holds as much vapor as it can at that temperature
The air is 100 degrees

wrong.B: The article does not say 100 percent means rain.
wrong.D: The number is a percent of water vapor, not a temperature.

questions.stem: Which places does the article name as sources of water that evaporates?
options: Seas, lakes, plants, and wet clothes
Only the Red Sea
Mountains, rocks, and the sand of the desert
Clouds and fog

questions.stem: Read this: "some vapor must condense, or turn back into tiny drops." What does condense mean here?

To change from liquid into gas
To become warmer
To change from gas into liquid

questions.stem: What happens right after air cools down?
options: It can hold more vapor
Some of its vapor condenses into drops
Its relative humidity drops all the way down to zero percent
The water evaporates faster
questions.why: Cool air holds less vapor, so some of it condenses into drops like dew.

wrong.A: Cool air holds less vapor, not more.
wrong.C: Cooling makes relative humidity go up, toward full.
wrong.D: Evaporation is slower in cool, damp air.

questions.stem: A glass of cold juice gets wet on the outside on a humid day. Why?

Someone spilled water on it
Air touching the cold glass cools, and its vapor condenses
The glass is evaporating

questions.stem: Why would a runner probably feel worse in Dammam in summer than in Riyadh on a day with the same temperature?

Riyadh has more sweat in the air
Dammam is higher in the mountains

questions.stem: How does the article mainly explain dew, clouds, and fog?
options: As a list of dates
As a story about one family
As three different causes
As results of the same cause: cooling air

MID.prompt: Explain how a puddle on the ground could later become part of a cloud. Use the words evaporate and condense.
checklist: I explained evaporation and condensation in order.
I used evaporate and condense correctly.
I included the role of warm and cool air.
MID.modelAnswer: First, warm sunlight heats the puddle, and the water begins to evaporate, turning from a liquid into invisible water vapor that rises into the air. As that moist air rises higher, it cools down, and cooler air cannot hold as much vapor, so the vapor begins to condense back into tiny drops. Those tiny drops gather together high in the sky and form a cloud.

keyWords.definition: the tiniest bits of a substance that are still that substance
keyWords.example: Water molecules spread out when water boils.

keyWords.definition: the change of a gas into a liquid, usually as it cools
keyWords.example: Condensation covered the bathroom mirror after a hot shower.

keyWords.definition: so full of something that it cannot take in any more
keyWords.example: The sponge was saturated, so water dripped out of it.

keyWords.definition: on or near the coast, where land meets the sea
keyWords.example: We drove along the coastal road beside the Gulf.
The museum uses a hygrometer to protect its old books from damp air.

questions.stem: Which sentence best states the central idea?
options: Humidity is invisible water vapor whose amount depends on temperature and which shapes weather and comfort
Nitrogen and oxygen make up most of the atmosphere
Laundry dries faster in the desert than beside the sea, so families in Riyadh rarely use dryers at home
Meteorologists prefer coastal cities
questions.why: The article explains what humidity is, how evaporation and condensation change it, and how it affects weather and people.

wrong.C: This is a possible inference, not the main idea.
wrong.D: The article does not say this.

As molecules drifting among nitrogen and oxygen molecules
As small pieces of ice
As dust that holds water

questions.stem: What does it mean when the air is saturated?

It is above 40 degrees
Its relative humidity is 100 percent and it cannot accept more vapor
It is full of dust and sand after a strong storm has blown through the city

questions.stem: Which detail best explains why dew forms by sunrise?
options: Grass makes water at night
Warm air holds more vapor, so chilly air near the grass must release some
Plants evaporate water from their leaves in the morning, and it falls back onto the grass
Fog falls onto the grass

wrong.C: Evaporation adds vapor; it does not make dew.

questions.stem: Why does a humid afternoon feel hotter than a dry one at the same temperature?
options: Humid air heats the skin directly
The sun shines more strongly through humid air, so the skin absorbs much more heat
Sweat evaporates more slowly, so less heat is carried away from the skin
The body stops producing perspiration

wrong.A: The article does not say humid air heats skin directly.

questions.stem: If the temperature rises in the afternoon but the amount of vapor stays the same, what happens to relative humidity?
options: It goes up to 100 percent
It stays exactly the same
It becomes saturated
It goes down, because warm air could hold more
questions.why: Relative humidity compares the vapor present with the maximum; warmer air has a higher maximum, so the percentage falls.

wrong.A: Warming moves the air away from saturation.
wrong.B: The maximum changes with temperature, so the percent changes.
wrong.C: Saturation happens with cooling, not warming.

questions.stem: What can you infer about coastal Jeddah compared with Riyadh?

Jeddah has no hygrometers
Riyadh has more water vapor in its air
Jeddah is colder all year
questions.why: The article links evaporation from seas to humidity and says coastal cities are humid while inland Riyadh is dry.

wrong.C: The article says Riyadh's air is dry.

To compare Saudi cities
Because water must first become vapor before it can condense back into droplets

wrong.B: Cities are compared at the end, not in this order.
wrong.D: The article does not explain how a hygrometer is built.

HIGH.prompt: Explain how humidity connects the sea, the sky, and the human body. Use evidence about evaporation, condensation, and sweat.
checklist: I explained both evaporation and condensation.
I connected humidity to how people feel.
I used at least two key words correctly.
HIGH.modelAnswer: Humidity connects the sea, the sky, and the human body through one continuous cycle of water molecules. Water evaporates from the sea and other sources, filling the air with vapor until it may even become saturated, and when that moist air cools, condensation turns the vapor back into drops that form dew, fog, or clouds. This same humidity also affects people: in coastal cities like Jeddah where the air holds more moisture, sweat evaporates slowly off the skin, so a humid day feels hotter and stickier than a dry one in Riyadh.
